transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, yeah… I guess the main thing is my eating’s gotten kind of out of hand. After late shifts, I’ll stop and get food—like a full takeout meal—and then when I get home I just keep going. Chips, sweets, whatever’s around in the apartment.

It’s weird because I work these odd hours, and by the time I’m done everything feels like it’s either closing or it’s all fast food, you know? I used to grab stuff after shifts with coworkers sometimes, but now it’s more like I’m by myself and I’ll eat way more than I meant to. Then afterward I kind of look at the wrappers or containers and I’m shocked, like… how did I eat all of that?
How do you feel after you've eaten all that food and seen the wrappers or containers?

I feel kind of stunned, honestly. Like I’ll see the takeout container and the chip bag and maybe candy wrappers, and it’s just… I don’t know, it doesn’t feel like I meant to eat all that.

After late shifts I’ll tell myself I’m just grabbing dinner, but then I get home and keep going with whatever’s around. And then I’m looking at it all afterward thinking, wow, that was a lot. It’s embarrassing, I guess. Also I hate wasting money on takeout—my apartment’s near this place that stays open late, and I keep saying I should just go straight home, but then… yeah. I end up shocked by how much I ate.
Do you feel guilty after eating all that food?

I mean… I don’t know if “guilty” is the exact word. I feel embarrassed, definitely, and kind of mad at myself, I guess. Like I’ll think, why did I spend money on all that when I’ve got groceries sitting there? I even bought those meal prep containers once—this whole plan to be organized—and they’re still in the cabinet.

So… yeah, maybe some guilt, but mostly it’s this uncomfortable, “ugh, why did I do that?” feeling.
Do you ever try to make up for eating a lot by doing something to counteract it?

Yeah… I guess I do. Not like, I don’t know, some big planned thing, but if I’ve had a really bad night with food, the next morning I’ll feel like I have to sort of fix it.

Like I’ll go run extra miles on the trail, even if I’m wiped out from work. There’s this trail near me that I usually like, actually—it’s kind of the one place I clear my head—but after those nights it doesn’t feel relaxing. It feels more like, “you have to do this because of what you ate.”

Or I’ll skip breakfast before my shift, which is dumb because then I’m tired and cranky at work, and dealing with customers when you’re hungry is… not great. But in my head it’s like I’m trying to undo the night before.
How often do you try to make up for eating a lot by doing something to counteract it?

Most weeks, I guess. Since I moved into this apartment and things kind of settled into a routine, it’s been… usually at least once a week there’s a late night where I eat way more than I meant to.

And then the next day—or sometimes that night—I try to make up for it somehow. Like skipping breakfast, making myself do a long run even if I don’t really want to, or… sometimes throwing up. I don’t like saying that. It’s not every single day or anything, but most weeks it happens at least once.
How often do you throw up after eating?

Sometimes. Not every time I eat too much, but… yeah, sometimes after I get home and it’s like I’ve had too much takeout or snacks, I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up.

It’s hard to explain because part of me knows it’s not… a normal thing to do, but in the moment I’m thinking I don’t want it just sitting in me, like it’s going to turn into weight. And then I feel gross about the whole thing.

I guess it happens on those bad nights, mostly. Not every day.
How many times a month do you throw up after eating?

Um… if I had to put a number on it, maybe like four times a month? Sometimes a little less, sometimes more, depending on how many of those nights happen.

It’s usually after I get home and I’ve eaten too much takeout or snacks, and then I get this panicky feeling like I don’t want it just sitting in me, like it’s going to turn into weight. So I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. I hate saying it that plainly, but… yeah, probably around once a week.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t like admitting that, but yes. Even when people at the venue say I look too lean or whatever, I still get really nervous if my pants feel a little tighter.

Like, I’ll be getting ready for a shift and if the waistband feels different, suddenly I’m thinking everybody’s going to notice. Guests, coworkers… like they’ll look at me and think I let myself go. It’s dumb because most people are probably just trying to find their seats or buy a drink, but in my head it feels really obvious.

And if the scale is up even a pound, it can kind of ruin my whole mood.
Do you think you would be upset if you gained weight even if it didn't affect your health?

Yeah… I think I would be. I mean, even if a doctor told me, “Your health is fine,” I’d still feel really upset if I gained weight.

It’s like at the venue, people will even say I look too lean sometimes, and I still don’t really believe it. If my pants feel tighter before a shift, I start getting panicky, like everyone’s going to notice right away — guests, coworkers, whoever — and think I let myself go. Or if the scale is up even a pound, it sticks in my head.

And then I’m distracted the whole night, even though I’m supposed to be helping people find seats or dealing with the usual chaos. So yeah… it would bother me, even if it wasn’t a health thing.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?

Um… significant? I don’t know. I don’t think there’s been some huge change, not that I’ve really noticed.

I mean, I check sometimes, but then I kind of get in my head about normal ups and downs, like if I ate late after a shift or had a bunch of salty food. The schedule at the venue is weird too, so it’s hard to tell what’s real and what’s just, you know, one bad day on the scale.

So… I’m not sure. Nothing dramatic that I can point to, I guess.
Do you think you look overweight even when others tell you that you're too lean?

Yeah… I guess I do, or at least I feel that way. Like, people at the venue have told me I look too lean, and I’ll kind of nod like, “yeah, okay,” but I don’t really take it in.

If my pants feel even a little tighter before a shift, my brain just goes straight to, like, everyone’s going to notice — coworkers, guests, whoever — and they’re going to think I let myself go. Which is ridiculous, because most guests are just asking where their seats are or complaining about drink prices, but I’m standing there thinking about my waistband.

And if the scale is up even a pound, it feels like proof, even if other people are telling me the opposite. So… yeah, I don’t think I see it the way they do.
Do you feel like you're eating excessively because you're afraid of gaining weight or because you feel like you've lost control over your eating?

Yeah… I think it’s more the losing control part. I mean, the weight thing is always kind of buzzing in the background, but on those nights when I start eating, it’s like I’m not fully in charge anymore.

Like I’ll tell myself, okay, just put the container away, go brush your teeth, go do literally anything else… and then I’m standing there opening another thing anyway. It feels almost like I’m watching myself do it from outside my body, which sounds dramatic, but that’s what it feels like.

And then suddenly everything’s gone, and I’m just sitting there thinking, why didn’t I stop? It’s not even like I’m enjoying it by the end.
How often do you have episodes where you feel like you've lost control over your eating?

Most weeks, I think… at least once. It got more noticeable after my apartment move kind of settled down, once I had a routine again. Which is funny, because I thought the routine would help, but late at night is when it happens.

I’ll mean to just have something small, and then it turns into way more than I planned. Like, past the point where I’m even hungry. And then I panic and try to make up for it — throwing up, or skipping breakfast the next morning, or making myself go on this long run even if I’m tired.

So… yeah. Usually once a week, sometimes more, but most weeks at least once.
How often do you make yourself throw up after one of these episodes of eating excessively?

Not every time, but… sometimes. Like if I get home and I’ve eaten way too much takeout or snacks, I’ll end up in the bathroom and make myself throw up.

It’s usually because I get this panicky feeling that it’s just going to sit in me and turn into weight. I know that probably sounds… I don’t know, irrational, but in the moment it feels like I have to get it out.
How often do you make yourself throw up after eating excessively?

Yeah… like I said, not every time, but sometimes after I get home and I’ve eaten too much—usually takeout or snacks, stuff that’s just there—I’ll go into the bathroom and make myself throw up.

It’s hard to explain because part of me knows it’s not a normal reaction, but in my head it’s like, if I don’t get it out, it’s just going to sit there and turn into weight. And then I get stuck on that thought.

Sorry, I know I’m kind of circling around it. The short answer is: sometimes.
How often do you make yourself throw up after an episode of eating excessively?

Right… yeah, sorry, I know you asked that already. It’s not after every time I overeat, but sometimes, especially if I get home and I’ve had too much takeout or snacks. I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up.

It’s like I get stuck on the idea that if it stays in me, it’s going to turn into weight. I know that probably doesn’t sound logical, but in the moment it feels really urgent.
Do you make yourself throw up after every episode of eating excessively?

No, not every time. It’s more like… sometimes, usually after I get home and I’ve had too much takeout or snacks. I’ll get this thought stuck in my head that it’s just sitting in me and it’s going to turn into weight, and then I end up going to the bathroom and making myself throw up.

I know you’re asking a pretty simple yes-or-no thing—so, no, not every episode. Just sometimes.
Do you make yourself throw up every time you have an episode of eating excessively?

No, not every time. It’s more… sometimes, like after I get home and I’ve eaten too much takeout or snacks, and then I start thinking about it sitting in my stomach. I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up because I get scared it’s just going to turn into weight.

I know I’ve probably said that a few times—I just get kind of stuck on explaining it.
Is making yourself throw up something you do more often than not after eating excessively?

I’d say… not more often than not, no. It’s sometimes. Like if I get home and I’ve had too much takeout or I keep eating snacks, then my head starts going, you know, like it’s just sitting there and it’s going to become weight.

And then I’ll end up in the bathroom making myself throw up. But it’s not every time, or most times exactly… it’s more when that panic feeling kicks in.
Do you make yourself throw up at least once a week after eating excessively?

Yeah… I think it can be at least once a week sometimes. Like, if I come home after work and I’ve grabbed takeout, and then I keep picking at snacks too, I start thinking about it just sitting in me. It sounds kind of ridiculous when I say it out loud, but I get scared it’s going to turn into weight.

So I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. Not every single time I overeat, but yeah, sometimes it happens around once a week.
